rationale: This is a single-denominator swap (at → lt) on the archive's already-tested "Cash Earnings After Mandatory Outflows" (alpha 5.2%, t 4.45) with the operator, distress leg and sample deliberately held fixed — the definition of a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism, and lt-scaling also introduces a mechanical blow-up for low-liability firms that the proposal does not address.

target_name: Funding Horizon Pooled With Maturity Structure
rationale: Pooling runway with maturity concentration into a single SUMRANK distress leg is a legitimate and internally consistent recombination of two independently validated dimensions, but it reuses a design template already run in the archive ("Conjunction With Broad Liquidity Leg") and the two pooled components are less orthogonal than claimed since dlc sits in both the maturity ratio and the firms' near-term cash needs.

This is "Cash Survival Against The Maturity Wall" with oancf/at replaced by (oibdp−xint−txt)/at — a profitability-leg substitution already shown elsewhere in the archive to be near-equivalent — and it is additionally redundant with proposal #2 in the same batch, so at best it is a coverage-diagnostic rerun rather than a new hypothesis.

A scale-free accounting distance-to-default that puts earnings volatility where structural models put it (denominator of a cushion) is genuinely distinct from everything in the archive and internally coherent, though it flirts with the published distance-to-default/earnings-volatility literature and mixes a flow (xint) with a stock (dlc) in the fixed-charge threshold, and small-VOL denominators will demand more than WINSOR to tame.

target_name: Profitability Slope Flip Across Leverage States
rationale: The indicator algebra correctly produces a +1/−1 contrast (low leverage <0.3 vs high leverage >0.3) that matches the stated hypothesis and expected sign, and swapping only the state variable is a clean discriminating test of whether the earlier flip result is about funding horizon or distress generally — but it is a near-clone of an existing archive signal and directly contradicts the gen-0 leverage-gated profitability priors that already failed, so the prior on a null is high.

Sign and construction are consistent (product of two badness ranks, expected negative), and the creditor-priced hazard is informationally distinct from the accrual and maturity legs already tried, but this is now the third instance of the identical "NEG(runway) × hazard rank" template and xint/lt is a noisy cost-of-debt proxy that is mechanically diluted by non-debt liabilities, so a strong result will be hard to attribute to the claimed refinancing-cost channel rather than to leverage.
